habitats: Protected western benches and gullies between 80 and 950 m
summary: A 12–22 m evergreen of the sheltered western fog belt. Grooved leaves intercept fog, while stout trunks, conditional buttresses and flexible crowns resist wind loading. Red-veined leaves advertise alkaloids; soft green-gold fruit feeds rondo. Normal stands are absent from exposed ridgelines (F4, F8, F18, F19, F25).

chains.trait: Grooved leaves and elongated drip tips
links: Western fog deposits suspended droplets onto foliage.
Beads merge and drain through grooves.
Drip tips deliver intercepted water to litter and shallow roots.
chains.play: Locate morning canopy drip and humid understory patches.
chains.weakness: Clear weather removes the fog-water subsidy.
observe: Litter beneath branch tips darkens first.

plausibility.summary: Leaves collect existing droplets; pressure does not generate water. Mature stands remain within the sheltered western fog belt.

analogues.mechanism: Canopy interception supplies fog water to soil and understory; grooved leaves are a fictional extension.

links: Dense-air winds load the crown strongly.
Wet shallow soils can limit deep anchorage.
Buttresses spread overturning forces while flexible branches reduce loading.
Sheltered terrain permits tall stands that exposed ridges cannot sustain.
chains.play: Use buttress hollows and branch forks for cover or climbing; inspect damage before trusting a route.
chains.weakness: Undercutting, loose saturated soil, heavy vines and exposed ridge winds can overwhelm support.
observe: Trees in shallow wet hollows have large flares.
Trees on deep drained soil have smaller flares.
Tall stands stop below an exposed ridgeline.

plausibility.summary: Buttresses address anchorage rather than oxygen abundance. Generate normal 12–22 m trees only in sheltered stands; exclude exposed ridges instead of generating full-height windproof trees.

analogues.mechanism: Buttress roots resist overturning; crown flexibility provides an additional means of reducing load.

food_for: Frugivores and omnivores eating ripe fruit
gameplay.gift_item: Soft green-gold fog fruit for rondo

poison.signal: Red-purple veins mark defended leaves; fruit ripeness uses softness and scent.

gameplay.cover: Buttress hollows, shaded trunks and low branches.
gameplay.nest_material: Fallen twigs and shed epiphytic fibres.
gameplay.notes: Ripe pulp is edible despite defended foliage. Fog drip does not guarantee pure drinking water. Normal forest and canopy routes end before exposed ridges.

relations.note: Carries seeds from fallen fruit at accessible forest margins.
Uses sheltered branch forks for nests and launch points.
Finds shade without gaining tolerance to defended leaves.
Supports damp cushions on sufficiently illuminated bark.
Supports vines whose added weight and foliage can burden the host.
Fog drip sustains humid understory patches.

generator.trunk: Stout tapering trunk with vertically furrowed grey-brown bark.

branching.buttress: Prominent on shallow saturated soil; subdued on deep drained soil.

leaf.type: Narrow elliptic evergreen blade with drainage grooves and drip tip

colour.base: Deep green foliage and grey-brown bark
overlay_rules: Ripe fruit becomes soft dull green-gold.

placement.slope: Sheltered western benches, lower gullies and moderate slopes; exclude exposed ridgelines, summit crests and failing cliffs.
placement.wetness: Persistently humid, with locally saturated rooting pockets.
placement.soil: Developed volcanic soil with litter and variable rooting depth.
placement.density: Sheltered stands interrupted by streams, storm gaps and exposed terrain; no normal-height ridge instances.

generator.seasonal: Evergreen; favourable moisture supports foliage and fruit production. Storms create branchfall and canopy gaps.
generator.wind_response: Flexible outer branches bend leeward; exposed ridges are excluded from mature-tree placement.

journal.en: The leaves comb water from passing fog. Sweet fruit below; bitter red veins above.
journal.es: Las hojas peinan el agua de la niebla. Abajo, fruta dulce; arriba, nervios rojos y amargos.

observe: Red veins remain visible in green leaves.
Tall crowns disappear before the exposed ridge.
secrets: Damp litter can reveal an unseen overhanging crown.
Fruit visitors identify accessible forest margins.
Large buttresses reveal shallow wet rooting ground vulnerable after storms.
